contracts.description: The work-store transition contract: create/claim/unclaim/close/reopen/delete/update/comment/link/unlink mutations and show/list/search/ready/report/export/import windows, with each task's plain summary and owner's ask (it-ts-plain) and where it came from (it-ts-source), as pure transitions over (state, command) proven by op-sequence fixtures; and, for a binding that persists the store, no acknowledged write lost to concurrent writers (it-ts-durable).

exclusions: The loom boundary: memory, knowledge, identity, and prose-wiki surfaces belong to the owner's memory layer, never the work store. This contract offers no surface for them; a conforming store and its tooling add none (the judgment criterion ac-ts-loom-boundary carries the refusal).

Storage engine and persistence: SQLite, WAL, file locations, and the write cadence of any passive on-disk export mirror are binding surface. The export CONTENT is contract (it-ts-portability); the file is not.
CLI and MCP surface: verb spellings, flags, output formatting, trees, emoji, and human-facing rendering are binding surface; only the command/result values are contract.

Sync, federation and remotes: one store, held in one place. Concurrent writers on that one store are NOT excluded (0.6.0, t-1831): a binding that persists the store and lets more than one process write it carries it-ts-durable. How it serializes them (a database lock, a file lock, one writer process) is binding surface.

Id generation scheme beyond the judgment criterion ac-ts-id-shape: random suffixes, dotted children, and sequences are implementation surface. Fixture corpora place caller-supplied ids in a 'legacy-' namespace and assume generated ids never collide with them; a generator emitting ids in that namespace fails those fixtures spuriously.

Deferred, not refused (arrive as proposed criteria via promotion if wanted): defer/snooze and a deferred status, labels/tags, stats and dashboards, stale/orphan hygiene tooling, batch mutations, and re-alerting/notification of any kind. (delete and search were on this list through 0.1.0; 0.2.0 promotes them into the contract — it-ts-lifecycle and it-ts-query. unlink was deferred through 0.2.0; 0.3.0 promotes it into it-ts-links.)

Automation around the store: hooks, timers, Discord delivery, audit-trail rendering of actor/at on mutations that do not stamp observable fields (update, comment metadata beyond the comment record, import's envelope actor/at) — recorded or not as the binding pleases; not observable here.
Actor identity and authentication: actor is a free-form attribution string with no semantics (felag-tasks precedent).

Import stamp cross-consistency: import validates identity, vocabulary, timestamps, and link structure; whether a closed record carries closedAt or an in_progress record carries startedAt is the exporter's business — records are held verbatim.

felag-tasks conformance is proven by running the c-tasks fixture corpus over a WorkLayer projection of this store, not restated here; it-ts-create's linkage idempotency and it-ts-query's report op are the store-side support that makes that layer mapping-only.

Residue: a float-integer-lexeme priority (2.0) is normative in prose — a priority is its mathematical value, so 2.0 is the valid priority 2 — but unfixturable in this interchange: a JSON serializer that canonicalizes numbers writes 2.0 as 2, so the adversarial lexeme cannot survive into a fixture. A genuinely fractional value (2.5) survives canonicalization and is fixtured (fx-priority-fractional).

Residue: report's tertiary taskRef sort key is unfixturable by construction — linkage uniqueness means two spec-linked tasks can never share (specItemRef, criterionId), so the tertiary comparison is never decisive; it is retained verbatim for c-tasks alignment (it-ts-query).

The plain-words lint: which words a title, goal or ask may not use (ids, lane words, site codes), and whether a binding refuses or only warns, is binding policy. This contract holds the plain fields verbatim and judges no wording (it-ts-plain).
goals: Carry exactly the working surface six months of agent-driven tracking actually used — ready queue, parent/child containers, priorities, claim/close lifecycle, comments, ad-hoc and spec-linked tasks — and refuse the junk drawer loudly.

The core is one pure transition function over (state, command): the clock and the actor ride in the command, queries are the only observable, and every behavior is fixtured; storage, CLI, and scheduling live in bindings.

The exit door is contract, not convention: lossless live export and identity-preserving import are fixture-carried MUSTs — the property the previous tracker's passive export promised and was probed not to hold (stale and lossy, 2026-06-12).
Native felag-tasks support: linkage-idempotent create and the report projection make the c-tasks WorkLayer over this store mapping-only.
name: taskstore-core

body:
The taskstore core is one total transition function, apply: (state, command) -> (result, state). Every mutating command carries its own clock (at) and attribution (actor); the store never reads a wall clock and never invents attribution, so a command sequence determines every observable exactly. State is never exposed: it is observable only through the query commands — show, list, ready, report, search, export — and through the fields each mutation's own result envelope carries (created, id, linked, removed, imported).

Wire format taskstore/op-sequence@0: input is {ops: [command, ...]}, executed in order against an initially empty store; expected is {results: [result, ...]}, one result per command, compared by structural JSON equality (key-order-independent) after id normalization. Id normalization: $k denotes the id generated by the k-th create command in the sequence that returns created true — $1 the first actual creation, $2 the second, counting neither failed creates nor idempotent hits. In command inputs a $-token resolves to that generated id before the command runs; a token or id string naming no held task reaches validation as an unknown referent, never as a parse error. Tokens resolve only in the id-valued fields: id, dependsOn, parent, and the id and dependsOn of each import links entry. In results, every string equal to a generated id is rendered as its token, wherever it appears; ids supplied by the caller (import) are literal in both inputs and results, except an imported id equal to an id generated earlier in the same sequence, which renders as that token like every other occurrence of the id.

Ids are opaque strings, unique among held tasks. A generated id is never reused: it differs from every id the store has ever held, deleted ones included — imported ones too, so an import of an id the generator could produce moves the generator past it. An imported id collides only with HELD ids (E_DUP_ID, it-ts-portability), so an id freed by delete may return by import; beyond that and the judgment criterion ac-ts-id-shape, the generation scheme is the implementation's. actor is a free-form attribution string with no semantics.

Timestamps: every at-valued field is an RFC 3339 date-time, parseable exactly as felag-core it-verification's Timestamps rule defines (numeric offset or Z required, T and Z case-insensitive, second 60 excluded) — that rule is incorporated by reference, not restated. A required timestamp field that is absent or not a string is E_MISSING_FIELD; a string that does not parse is E_BAD_TIMESTAMP. Accepted timestamps are stored and returned VERBATIM: this contract never normalizes to UTC and never orders anything by timestamp value — every ordering it defines is submission or creation order — so offset spelling can never change observable output beyond the verbatim field itself.

Results are envelopes with exact key sets. Every result carries ok (boolean) and errors (array); create adds created and id; link adds linked; unlink adds removed; show adds task; list, ready, report and search add entries; export adds tasks and links; import adds imported. On error the payload fields hold neutral values: id null, created false, linked false, removed false, task null, entries [], imported 0 (export takes no arguments and cannot error, so tasks and links have no error case). errors is a sorted set — ascending code-point order, deduplicated — and validation is all-applicable, never short-circuiting: every well-posed check reports its code. Well-posedness: field-validity checks (presence, type, vocabulary, timestamp parse) are always well-posed and co-fire. Referent-existence checks are well-posed over STRING-valued referent fields only, and then co-fire: a referent field that fails its type check reports its type error (E_BAD_FIELD, or E_MISSING_FIELD when required) alone — no existence lookup happens on a non-string, so a numeric parent never adds E_UNKNOWN_ID. Checks that interrogate an existing referent and can REFUSE — transition legality, cycle detection, parent uniqueness — are gated ONLY by what they interrogate: each evaluates whenever its referents exist (and, for link's graph checks, whenever the type names a known graph), and CO-FIRES with any field errors elsewhere in the command. The two referent-interrogating SUCCESS paths are different: duplicate-link detection and linkage idempotency divert a command to its no-op/hit envelope only when the command validates clean — a command reporting any error never reaches them (it-ts-create, it-ts-links). An unparseable at never suppresses E_BAD_TRANSITION on a known referent; an unknown referent suppresses exactly the checks that needed it. A command reporting any error changes nothing: per-command atomicity. Field-validity rules shared by every command: a required field absent or not of its declared type is E_MISSING_FIELD; an optional field present but not of its declared type is E_BAD_FIELD. Exception: type-valued fields (E_BAD_TYPE) and priority (E_BAD_PRIORITY) carry their own codes for ANY present-but-invalid value — unknown string, wrong JSON type, out-of-range — wherever they appear and whether required or optional; only ABSENCE of a required type or priority is E_MISSING_FIELD. A command whose op is absent or names no command in this contract returns exactly {ok: false, errors: [E_BAD_FIELD]} and changes nothing. Error codes (the set is unchanged since 0.1.0): E_BAD_FIELD, E_BAD_PRIORITY, E_BAD_TIMESTAMP, E_BAD_TRANSITION, E_BAD_TYPE, E_CYCLE, E_DUP_ID, E_DUP_LINKAGE, E_HAS_PARENT, E_MISSING_FIELD, E_UNKNOWN_ID.

The store holds work tracking only: memory, knowledge, and identity live in the owner's memory layer, and this contract deliberately offers no surface for them — the boundary that is not enforced is the boundary that erodes (see the exclusions and ac-ts-loom-boundary).
interfaceSketch: apply(state: StoreState, command: Command): {result: Result, state: StoreState} — pure, total, no I/O; op-sequence runner folds apply over ops and normalizes generated ids to $-tokens.
title: The store as pure transitions

gherkin:
Given a command violating several independent field-validity and referent-existence rules at once
When it runs
Then errors carries every applicable code exactly once, sorted ascending — never just the first failure — and the store is unchanged
And an absent or unknown op reports E_BAD_FIELD in the bare envelope

Given parseable non-Z-offset and lowercase-designator timestamps on create, claim, close, comment, and imported records, plus offsetless and leap-second forms
When they run
Then every accepted at-valued field — createdAt, startedAt, closedAt, comment ats, imported stamps — is returned verbatim through show and export, never normalized to UTC on ANY field, and the offsetless and leap-second forms are rejected with E_BAD_TIMESTAMP, creating nothing
And out-of-range hour, day, month and offset fields are unparseable
And leap years follow the 100/400 rule and offset minutes are bounded

Given a sequence where failed creates and an idempotent hit precede later successful creates
When results are normalized
Then $k counts only creates that actually created — the first success after two failures is $1, and the create after an idempotent hit takes the next token, not the command index

item: Generated ids match <prefix>-<suffix>: prefix one or more lowercase ASCII letters, suffix one or more lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or dots, at most 24 characters in all (t-1, art-3kq, art-3kq.2 comply). They are opaque to every consumer, differ from every id the store has ever held, and are never reused; the generation scheme itself — random suffix, dotted child, sequence — is the implementation's business.

The store holds work-tracking records only. It offers no command, record field, or result key whose purpose is to hold memory (what happened to or was learned by its owner), knowledge (facts about the world), identity (who its owner is), or wiki prose, and no tooling that reads or writes the store adds one. A task's description and comments about the work itself are not such a surface. Those belong to the owner's memory layer — a separate store, which for this store's first owner is loom — and work records cite them by reference ([[slug]], paths, URLs) instead of copying them in. Judged by reading the command set and any tool built on the store: a surface whose purpose is one of the four fails.

body:
create takes {title, actor, at, description?, type?, priority?, parent?, specItemRef?, criterionId?, legacyRef?, goal?, why?, doneWhen?, ask?, ifYes?, ifNo?, answers?, source?} and returns {ok, errors, created, id}. Required: title, actor, at — strings (absent or mistyped: E_MISSING_FIELD; unparseable at: E_BAD_TIMESTAMP per it-ts-model). Optional string fields (description, parent, specItemRef, criterionId, legacyRef) present but non-string: E_BAD_FIELD. The plain fields (goal, why, doneWhen, ask, ifYes, ifNo, answers) validate and store per it-ts-plain, and source per it-ts-source.

Defaults and vocabulary: type defaults to task; the vocabulary is task | bug | feature | epic, anything else E_BAD_TYPE. priority defaults to 2; a valid priority is an integer 0..4 by mathematical value, not lexeme — fractional, negative, out-of-range, or non-numeric values are E_BAD_PRIORITY (the fractional lexeme is unfixturable residue; see the exclusions). Only epic carries contract semantics elsewhere (it-ts-ready); types are otherwise labels.

A successful create stores the task with status open, createdAt = at (verbatim), createdBy = actor, the given fields, and a fresh id (created true). parent, when present, must name a held task (else E_UNKNOWN_ID, co-firing with any field errors); on success the parent-child edge (id depends on parent) is created atomically with the task, exactly as if link had run — a fresh task has no prior parent and cannot complete a cycle, so no link-side code can arise. legacyRef is preserved verbatim wherever the task renders (show, export).

Spec linkage: specItemRef (by convention 'spec:<specName>/<itemId>') with optional criterionId. criterionId when the specItemRef KEY is absent is E_MISSING_FIELD — key-presence, not value-validity: a criterionId alongside a present-but-mistyped specItemRef reports only the type error. Linkage idempotency — the c-tasks rule, native: tasks are keyed on (specItemRef, criterionId), absent criterionId a distinct key value. VALIDATION PRECEDES IDEMPOTENCY: a create reporting any error — field or referent, an unknown parent included — does nothing and returns the error envelope (id null), even when its linkage key is held. A create that validates clean and whose key is already held is a HIT: it returns ok true, created false, and the EXISTING task's id, whatever that task's status — open, claimed, or closed — and changes nothing: the title, the parent (no edge is created), and every other field of the proposal are discarded whole. Creates with no specItemRef carry no key and never collide. Distinct criterionIds under one specItemRef are distinct tasks. Keys compare as exact (specItemRef, criterionId) pairs: an empty-string criterionId is a present value, distinct from an absent one, and no two different pairs are ever the same key.
title: create — intake, defaults, and spec linkage

gherkin:
Given a create carrying only title, actor, and at, and another carrying description, type bug, and priority 0
When each runs and is shown
Then the first holds type task, priority 2, status open, createdAt/createdBy from the command, and no description key
And the second holds exactly the fields it was given

Given a create naming a held task as parent and another naming an unknown id
When they run, and link is then exercised against the create-set edge
Then the first creates the task and the parent-child edge atomically — visible as parent in show, as a links entry in export, and to link itself: re-parenting is E_HAS_PARENT, re-linking the identical edge is a no-op, and a cycle through the create-set edge is E_CYCLE
And the second reports E_UNKNOWN_ID and creates nothing

Given creates with actor absent or numeric, a present-but-mistyped required field (a numeric title; a numeric at), a criterionId without specItemRef, mistyped optional fields (parent, legacyRef, specItemRef, criterionId), priorities of -1 and "high", and a boundary priority 4
When they run
Then the absent or mistyped required fields and the lone criterionId report E_MISSING_FIELD (co-firing with other field errors), mistyped optionals report E_BAD_FIELD with NO existence lookup on a non-string referent, the bad priorities report E_BAD_PRIORITY, the boundary 4 is accepted, and nothing failed is created
And a fractional priority is E_BAD_PRIORITY on create and on update

Given tasks held for a (specItemRef, criterionId) key in each status — open, in_progress, closed
When the same key is created again with a different title, with a known parent, with an unknown parent, and with an out-of-range priority
Then the clean re-creates return ok with created false and the existing id whatever the status, the holder's fields survive and NO parent edge is created (the colliding proposal is discarded whole), the unknown-parent and bad-priority creates fail with their error envelopes and id null (validation precedes idempotency — field and referent alike), and report still lists exactly one entry per key

Given creates for one specItemRef under criterionId A, criterionId B, and no criterionId, then a REPLAY of the criterion-less key, then two creates with no specItemRef at all
When report and list run
Then three distinct spec-linked tasks exist with the keyless entry sorting first, the criterion-less replay is an idempotent HIT on (specItemRef, absent) — absent criterionId is a key value, not no key — and the two no-specItemRef creates are distinct tasks that never collide
And an empty-string criterionId, and a space inside either key field, never makes two different pairs one key

body:
The stored status vocabulary is exactly open | in_progress | closed. blocked is never stored — it is a view derived from links (it-ts-ready) — and there is still no deferred status (excluded, deferred-not-refused).

claim {id, actor, at}: requires status open; sets status in_progress, assignee = actor, startedAt = at. unclaim {id, actor, at}: claim's inverse — requires status in_progress; returns the task to open and REMOVES assignee and startedAt, as reopen removes the close stamps. Taking a task back out of progress is therefore an ordinary transition, not a reason to delete and re-file it. close {id, actor, at, reason?}: requires status open or in_progress; sets status closed, closedAt = at, and closeReason = reason when present — a close without a reason removes any closeReason the task held (reason optional string; E_BAD_FIELD when present non-string); fields stamped by an earlier claim survive. reopen {id, actor, at}: requires status closed; returns the task to open and REMOVES startedAt, assignee, closedAt, and closeReason — the claim and close stamps do not survive a reopen; history that matters belongs in comments.

A lifecycle command whose target's status is outside its requirement reports E_BAD_TRANSITION: claiming a task already in_progress or closed, unclaiming anything not in_progress, closing a closed task, reopening anything not closed. Per it-ts-model, E_BAD_TRANSITION is a referent-interrogating check: it co-fires with field errors (a bad at and a bad transition both report) but is not evaluated when the id is unknown — E_UNKNOWN_ID reports alone with the field errors. A failed lifecycle command changes nothing: stamps and status hold their prior values exactly.

delete {id, actor, at}: removes the task from the store entirely — the escape hatch for an erroneously-created task, which no other command provides (close is a status, not a removal). E_UNKNOWN_ID on an unknown or unresolved id, reported alone with any field errors per it-ts-model. delete admits a task in any status (no E_BAD_TRANSITION) and cascades: every link the task held as either endpoint — blocks or parent-child — is dropped, so the graph stays consistent (a deleted blocker unblocks its dependents, a deleted parent frees its children). A failed delete changes nothing.
title: claim, unclaim, close, reopen, delete — the status walk

gherkin:
Given an open task created by one actor
When a DIFFERENT actor claims it
Then the task is in_progress with assignee = the claiming command's actor — never the creator, never a session default — and startedAt = the command's at, verbatim

Given a claimed task and a separate never-claimed open task
When close runs on each, once with a reason and once without
Then both are closed with closedAt stamped; the reasoned close carries closeReason and the claim stamps survive; the unreasoned close carries no closeReason key
And a close without a reason leaves no closeReason, so a stray imported reason cannot project as cancelled

Given a task that was claimed then closed with a reason
When reopen runs
Then the task is open with startedAt, assignee, closedAt, and closeReason all absent
And a second reopen reports E_BAD_TRANSITION

Given lifecycle commands whose targets are in the wrong status — re-claiming in_progress, claiming closed, closing closed, reopening in_progress — or unknown (literal or unresolved $-token), or addressed with invalid fields
When they run
Then wrong-status targets report E_BAD_TRANSITION, which CO-FIRES with field errors on a known target (a non-string reason and an offsetless at report alongside it) but never fires on an unknown id, and every failed command leaves status and stamps exactly as they were

Given a held task, a task that blocks another, an unknown id, and a delete with no id
When delete runs on each
Then the held task is removed — show reports E_UNKNOWN_ID and list no longer carries it; the blocker's removal cascades its link so the formerly-blocked task becomes ready; the unknown id reports E_UNKNOWN_ID; and the id-less delete reports E_MISSING_FIELD
And deleting a parent frees its child to take a new parent, and deleting a dependent drops its blocks edge from export
And delete, unlink and update still require actor and a parseable at
And a deleted task's generated id never returns: a later create gets a distinct id and the deleted token stays unknown
And an in_progress task and a closed task are each deleted with ok true
And absent at is E_MISSING_FIELD on delete

Given a claimed task, an open task, and a closed task
When unclaim runs on each, on an unknown id, with an unparseable at, with both at once, and with no actor
Then the claimed task returns to open with assignee and startedAt REMOVED — key-absence, not null — while the open and closed targets report E_BAD_TRANSITION and change nothing, the closed task keeping every stamp an earlier claim and close left on it; and the error plumbing matches its sibling verbs — E_UNKNOWN_ID alone for the unknown id, E_BAD_TIMESTAMP co-firing with E_BAD_TRANSITION on a held task, the transition check NOT evaluated when the referent is unknown, and a missing actor co-firing as the sorted pair E_BAD_TRANSITION + E_MISSING_FIELD

body:
ready takes no arguments and returns {ok, errors, entries}: every task that is workable now. A task is ready iff its status is open AND its type is not epic AND it has no unsatisfied blocker, where a blocker is unsatisfied iff the task holds a blocks edge whose dependsOn target's status is anything other than closed. So: in_progress tasks are taken, closed tasks are done, epics are containers — none appear; a blocker that is merely claimed (in_progress) still blocks; closing the blocker releases. parent-child edges NEVER gate readiness: children of open containers are workable, and a non-epic parent is itself workable alongside its children. The epic exclusion is a deliberate divergence from the brownfield predecessor, whose queue surfaced containers as noise (probed 2026-06-12).

Order: priority ascending (0 first), ties by creation order ascending — the order tasks entered the store, which the op sequence fully determines. Never by id (opaque, implementation-varying) and never by timestamp (it-ts-model). Entry shape, exactly: {id, priority, title, type}, plus goal exactly when held (it-ts-plain).
title: ready — the work queue

gherkin:
Given open tasks with mixed priorities whose at timestamps deliberately disagree with their creation order
When ready runs
Then entries are sorted by priority ascending, ties broken by creation order ascending — a createdAt-ordered or id-ordered queue diverges and does not conform
And imported literal ids whose id order disagrees with creation order still surface in creation order

Given an epic (even at priority 0), an in_progress task, and a closed task alongside an open task
When ready runs
Then only the open non-epic task appears

Given tasks with one and with two blocks edges to open blockers
When ready runs as blockers are claimed and closed one at a time
Then the dependent is absent while ANY blocker is open or merely claimed — blockers gate as a conjunction, never released on the first unblock — present only when every direct blocker is closed, and blocking is one edge deep (a closed direct blocker releases the head whatever the far upstream's status)

Given a non-epic task with a child linked parent-child
When ready runs
Then both parent and child appear — parent-child edges never gate readiness

body:
link {id, dependsOn, type, actor, at} records that task id depends on task dependsOn. Types: blocks | parent-child — type is required: absent is E_MISSING_FIELD, any present-but-invalid value (unknown string, non-string) is E_BAD_TYPE (the it-ts-model exception). Both id and dependsOn must name held tasks; unknown referents report E_UNKNOWN_ID — errors being a set, one code however many referents are unknown — and a non-string referent field reports E_MISSING_FIELD with no lookup and no graph checks.

The two types form SEPARATE directed graphs. A link whose addition would create a directed cycle within its own type's graph — including the self-link, a 1-cycle — reports E_CYCLE; an edge in one graph never contributes to a cycle in the other (a blocks edge a->b coexists with a parent-child edge b->a). parent-child additionally keeps a forest: a task already holding a parent-child edge to some parent refuses a parent-child edge to a DIFFERENT parent with E_HAS_PARENT. Parent-uniqueness and cycle detection CO-FIRE when both hold — a link that would both re-parent a parented task and close a parent-graph cycle reports the sorted pair E_CYCLE + E_HAS_PARENT; only duplicate detection suppresses them.

A link identical to one already held — same (id, dependsOn, type) triple — is accepted with ok true and linked false, and changes nothing: no duplicate edge appears anywhere. link returns {ok, errors, linked}: linked is true exactly when an edge entered the store, and false on the duplicate no-op and on every error. Duplicate detection precedes the parent-uniqueness and cycle checks: re-linking the identical parent edge is a no-op, never E_HAS_PARENT. Edges render in three places: show renders a task's blocks targets as dependsOn in edge-creation order and its parent-child target as parent; export renders every edge in creation order as {dependsOn, id, type} (it-ts-portability). unlink {id, dependsOn, type, actor, at} removes the edge that link records, and returns {ok, errors, removed}. Its validation is link's exactly — the same required fields, the same type vocabulary and its E_MISSING_FIELD / E_BAD_TYPE split, the same held-referent rule reporting E_UNKNOWN_ID once however many referents are unknown — because an inverse that accepts a command link would have rejected is not an inverse. No graph check applies: removing an edge can neither close a cycle nor give a task a second parent, so E_CYCLE and E_HAS_PARENT cannot arise.

An unlink naming no held edge is ACCEPTED with ok true and changes nothing, as link accepts the identical duplicate: unlink is idempotent on repeat, so replaying a mirror never fails on an edge that is already gone. The inverse is exact over HELD referents and is deliberately not total — delete cascades every edge its target held (it-ts-lifecycle), so an unlink replayed after its dependsOn was deleted reports E_UNKNOWN_ID rather than a quiet success. The referent rule outranks the symmetry, and no claim of totality is made.

The no-op is observable rather than silent: removed is true exactly when an edge left the store and false otherwise, standing to unlink as created stands to create, and riding the error envelope as false exactly as created does. link carries the same signal in linked. Four situations produce removed false — a repeat, reversed referents, the wrong type, an edge that never existed — and the envelope separates none of them from each other, only all of them from a real removal. A binding that treats 'asked to remove, removed nothing' as FAILURE is therefore conforming, and one that reports it as success is conforming too — the choice is binding surface and this contract does not make it. The same holds for link's duplicate no-op (linked false). The idempotency the acceptance buys is the CORE's: an op-sequence or an import replayed against a store where the edge is already gone does not fail. It is not a promise about any binding's exit status. Removing a parent-child edge orphans the child — show stops rendering parent, and the task is re-parentable; removing a blocks edge un-gates the dependent in ready (it-ts-ready).
title: link and unlink — typed dependencies

gherkin:
Given a task linked blocks to two targets in an order that disagrees with id order
When show and export run
Then show lists dependsOn in edge-creation order — never id order — and export carries every edge as {dependsOn, id, type} in creation order

Given a chain of blocks edges, a self-link attempt, and parent-child edges over the same tasks
When links that would close a directed cycle within one type's graph are attempted
Then each reports E_CYCLE, while an edge that is acyclic within its own graph is accepted even when the OTHER graph holds the reverse edge

Given a task with a parent
When a parent-child link to a different parent is attempted, and when a link would both re-parent it and close a parent-graph cycle
Then the first reports E_HAS_PARENT, the second reports the sorted pair E_CYCLE + E_HAS_PARENT — the checks co-fire — and show still names the original parent

Given a held blocks edge and a held parent-child edge
When each identical link is submitted again
Then both are accepted ok and nothing changes — one edge each in show and export, and the repeated parent edge is a no-op, never E_HAS_PARENT

Given links naming unknown referents and an unknown type
When they run
Then unknown referents report E_UNKNOWN_ID once however many are unknown, an unknown type co-fires E_BAD_TYPE, and no edge is recorded

Given a held blocks edge gating a task in ready and a held parent-child edge
When each is unlinked, the blocks unlink is then repeated, and the orphaned child is linked to a different parent
Then both removals report removed true and the store shows them — the dependent becomes ready, show stops rendering parent, and export carries neither edge; the repeat is accepted with removed false and changes nothing; and the re-parenting SUCCEEDS, so a removed parent-child edge leaves no residue that could later refuse E_HAS_PARENT

Given a single held blocks edge from one task to another
When unlink names the same pair with the referents REVERSED, and then the correct pair with the WRONG type, each while the edge is still held
Then each reports ok with removed false and export still carries the edge unchanged — the match is the (id, dependsOn, type) triple exactly, not the unordered pair and not the pair alone — and only the exact triple removes it

Given a store holding a blocks edge
When unlink runs with one unknown referent, with BOTH referents unknown, with no type, with an unknown type, with an unknown referent and unknown type at once, with a non-string referent, and with an unparseable at
Then it reports E_UNKNOWN_ID once however many referents are unknown, E_MISSING_FIELD for the absent type and for the non-string referent with no lookup, E_BAD_TYPE for the unknown type, the sorted pair E_BAD_TYPE + E_UNKNOWN_ID when both hold, and E_BAD_TIMESTAMP for the bad clock — every one with removed false, and the held edge survives all of them in export
And delete, unlink and update still require actor and a parseable at

Given a blocks edge whose dependsOn target is then DELETED, cascading the edge away
When the original unlink is replayed
Then it reports E_UNKNOWN_ID rather than a quiet accepted no-op — unlink is idempotent on repeat but NOT total across delete, and the held-referent rule outranks the link/unlink symmetry

body:
comment {id, text, actor, at}: text is a required string; a successful comment appends {actor, at, text} to the task's comments. Comments render everywhere in SUBMISSION order, never re-sorted by at: a comment carrying an earlier clock than its predecessor still renders after it — clock skew must not rewrite history (it-ts-model orders nothing by timestamp).

update {id, set, actor, at}: set is a JSON object carrying at least one of exactly title, description, priority, assignee, or source (it-ts-source), or a plain field (goal, why, doneWhen, ask, ifYes, ifNo, answers; it-ts-plain, which also says how an empty string clears one). set absent, not an object, or an object with no keys at all: E_MISSING_FIELD. Any key other than those: E_BAD_FIELD — a set whose only keys are outside those (for example {status}) reports E_BAD_FIELD alone. Values validate as create does — priority an integer 0..4 by value (E_BAD_PRIORITY), the string fields strings (E_BAD_FIELD). A successful update replaces exactly the named fields. update never touches status or any stamp (createdAt, createdBy, startedAt, closedAt, closeReason), and it works on a task of ANY status — annotating closed work is normal operation (a title or description gets corrected after the fact). Neither comment nor update affects readiness, linkage, or lifecycle.
title: comment and update — annotation without lifecycle

gherkin:
Given a task and two comments, the second carrying an at EARLIER than the first's
When show runs
Then comments render in submission order — the later-submitted, earlier-stamped comment last — with actor, at, and text verbatim

Given a comment naming an unknown id and a comment missing text
When they run
Then they report E_UNKNOWN_ID and E_MISSING_FIELD respectively and no comment is recorded

Given an open task
When update sets title, description, priority, and assignee, the task is closed, and a further update amends description
Then every named field holds its newest value, the update on the closed task succeeds, and status and stamps are exactly what the lifecycle commands set

Given updates with an empty set, a set naming status, and a set carrying an out-of-range priority and a non-string title
When they run
Then they report E_MISSING_FIELD, E_BAD_FIELD, and the sorted pair E_BAD_FIELD + E_BAD_PRIORITY respectively, and the task is unchanged
And delete, unlink and update still require actor and a parseable at

body:
show {id}: the task's full record, or E_UNKNOWN_ID with task null. The record's key set is exactly: always {comments, createdAt, createdBy, dependsOn, id, priority, status, title, type}; plus each of answers, ask, askedBy, assignee, closeReason, closedAt, criterionId, description, doneWhen, goal, ifNo, ifYes, legacyRef, parent, source, specItemRef, startedAt, why exactly when held — absence is key-absence, never null. comments in submission order (it-ts-annotate); dependsOn is the task's blocks targets in edge-creation order, [] when none; parent is the parent-child target when one is held.

list {status?}: entries for tasks in creation order — the order they entered the store, imports included (it-ts-portability). Entry shape: {id, priority, status, title, type}, plus parent and goal each exactly when held. The status filter, when present, must be one of open | in_progress | closed (else E_BAD_FIELD with entries []) and restricts entries to tasks of that status. No filter means every task, whatever its status.

report: the c-tasks projection, natively. Entries for every spec-linked task — every task holding a specItemRef — with shape {criterionId?, specItemRef, status, taskRef} where taskRef is the task's id, sorted ascending by (specItemRef, criterionId, taskRef), each key compared in Unicode code-point order, with absent criterionId before any present value (the empty string included) (under linkage uniqueness the taskRef key is never decisive — two spec-linked tasks cannot share a (specItemRef, criterionId) key, absent criterionId being a key value; the tertiary key is retained verbatim for c-tasks alignment). Status mapping: open -> open; in_progress -> in_progress; closed -> done, EXCEPT closed with closeReason exactly "cancelled" — full-string, case-sensitive — which maps to cancelled. Tasks without specItemRef never appear. This projection is the store-side half of felag-tasks conformance: a WorkLayer over this store maps propose to create, transition-to-cancelled to close with reason "cancelled", and report to report.

search {q, status?}: entries for tasks whose id, title, description, specItemRef, criterionId, legacyRef, goal, why, or ask contains q as a case-insensitive substring (query and field both lowercased by the Unicode full default lowercase mapping, locale-independent, Final_Sigma applied — ECMAScript String.prototype.toLowerCase) — the text retrieval list lacks (list filters only by status). Entry shape and creation order are list's; the optional status filter further restricts to that status (one of open | in_progress | closed, else E_BAD_FIELD with entries []). A missing or non-string q reports E_MISSING_FIELD with entries []. The spec-link fields are searchable, so a criterionId or specItemRef term finds its linked tasks.
title: show, list, report, search — the windows

gherkin:
Given a task created with every optional field and an unknown id
When show runs on each
Then the task renders with exactly the held keys — absent optionals omitted, never null — and the unknown id reports E_UNKNOWN_ID with task null

Given tasks in each status
When list runs unfiltered, filtered to open, and filtered to a value outside the vocabulary
Then unfiltered lists every task in creation order with statuses shown, the open filter restricts to open tasks, and the bad filter reports E_BAD_FIELD with no entries

Given spec-linked tasks across two specItemRefs, one keyless and one claimed, alongside an ad-hoc task
When report runs
Then only spec-linked tasks appear, sorted by (specItemRef, criterionId, taskRef) with the keyless entry first, statuses projected to the c-tasks vocabulary
And keys compare in Unicode code-point order, not case-folded, locale-collated, or UTF-16 code-unit order

Given closed spec-linked tasks with closeReason "cancelled", "shipped", and "Cancelled"
When report runs
Then exactly the lowercase-"cancelled" task projects to cancelled and the others project to done — the match is full-string and case-sensitive

Given tasks whose text-bearing fields carry distinct terms — a title, and a criterionId on a spec-linked task
When search runs for a title term, for an UPPERCASED criterionId (case-insensitive), for a term in no task, and with no query at all
Then each field term returns exactly its carrying task in list shape, the uppercased query still hits the criterionId, the no-match returns no entries, and the missing query reports E_MISSING_FIELD with entries []
And case folds on both the query and the stored text, description, specItemRef, legacyRef and id are all reached, the status filter restricts, and a missing q with a bad status co-fires both codes
And a term held only in a comment, closeReason, assignee, createdBy, type, or status finds nothing

body:
Every task may carry a plain summary and, when a person must answer something, the owner's ask. They exist because a task list is read by people who did not write it (Jonathan, 2026-11-04: "if I can't understand it from the task list, I can't know if we're doing the right thing").

The summary: goal (what is true when the task is done), why (one line: why it matters), doneWhen (how we'll know). The ask: ask (the one question or request a person answers), ifYes and ifNo (what happens either way), and answers, one of exactly yes-no | words (how it's answered). why serves both: the reason the work matters is the reason given beside the ask. All are optional strings, held and rendered verbatim (show, export); none is required and none changes readiness, lifecycle or linkage.

Validation, on create, update's set and each import record alike: a plain field present but not a string is E_BAD_FIELD; answers, when a non-empty string, must be yes-no or words, else E_BAD_FIELD. ifYes, ifNo and answers are held only beside an ask: a create giving any of them non-empty with no non-empty ask is E_MISSING_FIELD, and so is an update giving any of them non-empty to a task that holds no ask and whose set gives none (key-presence of the ask decides, as criterionId's rule does in it-ts-create).

Writes: on create, a plain field given as the empty string is as if absent. On update, a plain field set to a non-empty string replaces it; set to the empty string, it is removed (key-absence, per it-ts-query) — and clearing ask also removes ifYes, ifNo, answers and askedBy, since they are held only beside it. askedBy is a stamp, never set directly: a create holding an ask, and every update setting a non-empty ask, sets askedBy to that command's actor — so an answer can go back to whoever asked. import holds askedBy verbatim (a string, else E_BAD_FIELD).

Windows: show and export carry every plain field and askedBy exactly when held. list, search and ready entries carry goal exactly when held, so a queue reads as what each task is for. search also matches goal, why and ask (it-ts-query).

Which words are plain is not this contract's: a binding may lint titles, goals and asks and refuse or warn (see the exclusions).
title: goal, why, doneWhen and the owner's ask — the plain words

gherkin:
Given a task created with goal, why and doneWhen, and one created with an empty goal
When show, list, ready and search run
Then show returns the three fields verbatim, list, ready and search entries carry goal, and the other task carries none of the keys

Given a task created with ask, ifYes, ifNo and answers by one actor
When another actor's update sets a new ask and answers, and a record with every plain field and askedBy is imported
Then askedBy is each ask-setting command's actor, the other fields hold verbatim, and export returns the imported record whole

Given an empty store
When create, update or import gives ifYes, ifNo or answers with no ask, answers outside yes-no and words, or a plain field that isn't a string
Then each reports E_MISSING_FIELD or E_BAD_FIELD as the rule says, and the store is unchanged

Given a task holding every plain field
When an update replaces goal and clears doneWhen with an empty string, and a later update clears ask
Then goal is the new value, doneWhen is absent, why is untouched, and ifYes, ifNo, answers and askedBy are absent with the ask

title: source — where a task came from
body:
A task may say where it came from: source, one string of the form <kind>:<value> — a kind of 1 to 32 characters in all, each a lowercase ASCII letter a-z, a digit 0-9 or -, the first a letter; a colon; then a value of 1 to 200 characters, none of them whitespace. Lengths count UTF-16 code units, as ECMAScript's String length does; whitespace is what ECMAScript's \s matches (Unicode White_Space and the line terminators, so U+00A0 and U+3000 count). So the whole rule is the ECMAScript pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}:\S{1,200}$. conversation:cv-0123456789ab names the conversation an agent made or changed the task in (loom docs/specs/comms.md, "Made here"); other kinds are a binding's. It exists so a thread can show the work it caused, and a task can say which thread it came from (Jonathan, 2026-11-05).

Validation, on create, update's set and each import record alike: source present but not a string, or a non-empty string not of that form, is E_BAD_FIELD. On create, an empty source is as if absent. On update, a non-empty source replaces the held one and an empty one removes it (key-absence, per it-ts-query). An import record's source must be a non-empty string of the form, since a held source never is: a non-string, empty or malformed one is E_BAD_FIELD, as on create (not E_MISSING_FIELD, the mistyped-string-field code of it-ts-portability). source is held and rendered verbatim (show, export); it changes no readiness, lifecycle or linkage, and list, ready and search entries never carry it, and search never matches it (it is not among it-ts-query's search fields). Finding the tasks of one source is export plus a filter: the contract has no window for it.

Which source a command carries is the binding's: a CLI may fill it from its environment (the conversation a body runs in) and keep the first one a task got. The contract holds what it's given.

gherkin:
Given a task created with a conversation source and one created with an empty source
When show, export, list, ready and search run (search for a term found only in a source), and updates set a source on the second, replace the first's, then clear it with an empty string
Then show returns each source verbatim when held and omits the key otherwise, export carries the same, no list, ready or search entry carries source, and the source-only term finds nothing

Given an empty store
When create or update gives a source that is not a string, has no colon, an empty or 33-character kind, a kind starting with a digit or -, a capital letter, an empty or 201-character value, or whitespace (a space, U+00A0) in the value, and creates give a 32-character kind with digits and -, and a 200-character value
Then each bad one reports E_BAD_FIELD and changes nothing, and the two at the bounds are held

Given an empty store
When a record carrying a source is imported, then records with an empty, a malformed or a non-string source
Then the first is held with its source verbatim and returned whole by export, and each later import reports E_BAD_FIELD alone with imported 0

body:
export takes no arguments and returns {ok, errors, tasks, links}: the store's complete observable content. tasks holds every held task in creation order, each in the show shape MINUS the derived keys parent and dependsOn — edges live once, in links — with comments always present ([] when none) and every other optional key exactly when held. links holds every edge in creation order, shape {dependsOn, id, type}. Export is total and live: every contract field a task holds appears, every time. An export that summarizes, truncates, or lags the store does not conform — the brownfield motivation for this contract: the predecessor's passive export was probed stale (24 of 45 issues) and lossy (no descriptions) on 2026-06-12.

import {tasks, links?, actor, at} accepts export-shaped content. The envelope actor and at are required and validate per the shared rules (E_MISSING_FIELD / E_BAD_TIMESTAMP); their values are not observable in this contract — audit recording is the binding's business (see the exclusions). Required per task record: createdAt, createdBy, id, priority, status, title, type — absence is E_MISSING_FIELD; present-but-invalid values follow the shared rules (the it-ts-model exception included): type E_BAD_TYPE and priority E_BAD_PRIORITY for ANY invalid present value, status non-string or outside open | in_progress | closed E_BAD_FIELD, the string fields mistyped E_MISSING_FIELD, and every timestamp field present — createdAt, startedAt, closedAt, comment ats — parseable (E_BAD_TIMESTAMP). Optionals as create accepts (source non-empty, per it-ts-source), plus assignee, askedBy (a string), startedAt, closedAt, closeReason, and comments ([{actor, at, text}], each field a required string). A task record carrying parent or dependsOn keys is E_BAD_FIELD — edges arrive only via links. Any other key outside a task record's fields (the show key set minus parent and dependsOn), and any key outside {actor, at, text} on a comment, is ignored: it is never stored and never rendered. E_DUP_ID checks held ids only, so an id freed by delete may be imported again (it-ts-model). Id collisions — within the payload or against any held id — report E_DUP_ID; linkage-key collisions (it-ts-create) likewise E_DUP_LINKAGE, checked only on a record whose specItemRef is a string and whose criterionId is absent or a string (a mistyped key field reports its type error alone, per it-ts-model's well-posedness). links entries validate as link does — minus actor and at, which an export-shaped entry {dependsOn, id, type} does not carry and import does not require — over the union of held and payload ids and against the held graph. They apply in payload order: an entry that validates clean joins the graph every later entry is checked against (so two payload parents for one task is E_HAS_PARENT), an entry identical to a held or earlier payload edge is an accepted no-op, and an entry that reports any error never joins. A task record, a comment, or a links entry that is not a JSON object reports E_MISSING_FIELD. Stamp cross-consistency is NOT validated: whether a closed record carries closedAt is the exporter's business (see the exclusions); records are held verbatim.

Import is ATOMIC: any error anywhere in the payload reports the full sorted error set with imported 0 and the store unchanged. On success, imported is the number of task records, ids are held literally — never regenerated — legacyRef and every field survive verbatim, and creation order extends by payload order. Round trip: importing an export into an empty store and exporting again yields the imported records exactly.
title: export and import — the exit door

gherkin:
Given a task carrying every optional field, a claim, and a comment, alongside a plain task and a blocks edge
When export runs
Then every held field of every task appears verbatim in creation order and the edge appears in links — nothing summarized, nothing dropped

Given an import of export-shaped records with literal legacy ids, stamps, multi-comment arrays, spec linkage, and parent-child and blocks links
When the store is queried through every window
Then the records are held verbatim under their literal ids in payload order, imported open tasks surface in ready and imported blocks edges gate it, imported spec-linked tasks project through report, and a clean create against an imported linkage key is a HIT returning the literal imported id — imported tasks are full store members
And an id freed by delete may return by import, and unknown keys on task records and comments are dropped
And payload links validate against held ids and the held graph, in payload order, with only clean entries joining it
And a repeated entry inside one payload is a no-op, not E_HAS_PARENT and not a second edge

Given imports whose payloads collide with held ids and linkage keys, repeat ids internally, violate vocabulary and timestamp rules, omit required fields, carry forbidden parent keys, or link unknown referents
When they run
Then every applicable code reports in one sorted set with imported 0 and the store holds exactly what it held before — per-record validation is not optional
And each per-record rule reports its code when it is the payload's only defect
And a mistyped criterionId never reaches the linkage-collision lookup
And a record missing only one required field, a comment missing only actor or at, an envelope missing only at, and a non-string record type each report their own code

Given an empty store
When an export-shaped payload is imported and export runs
Then the exported tasks and links equal the imported payload exactly — the exit door is lossless in both directions

body:
A binding that persists the store and admits more than one writer process at a time (agents and lanes write in parallel) applies each mutation to the state as the last writer committed it, and commits it whole or not at all. A mutation it acknowledges (ok true) is in the store afterwards, whatever other writers did meanwhile; a mutation it cannot apply (the store is locked past its wait, the disk is full, the write fails) reports ok false — never ok true — and changes nothing. Reads may run beside writes and see some committed state.

The failure this rules out was measured, not imagined: on 2026-11-04 five processes ran update, comment and close at once on the live store, and about 20 of roughly 450 writes reported ok and were not in the store afterwards (t-1831). The binding read the whole state outside its write transaction and wrote the whole state back from that copy, so a write that landed in between was overwritten.

Evidence is a taskstore/concurrent-writers@0 fixture: input {writers, opsPerWriter, sharedTasks} seeds sharedTasks tasks and one task per writer, then starts writers processes at once, writer w's i-th op being, by i mod 3: comment text "w<w>-i<i>" on shared task (w+i) mod sharedTasks; update description "w<w>-i<i>" on writer w's own task; close, reason "w<w>-i<i>", of a task created for that op. The result lists every acknowledged write the store does not hold afterwards: a comment not held exactly once, a close whose task is not closed with that reason, a writer's own task whose description is not that writer's last acknowledged update. expected is {lost: []}. Where in the binding the writers' processes enter (its storage layer, its CLI) is the binding's choice; each one must be its own OS process.
title: concurrent writers — no acknowledged write is lost

gherkin:
Given a persisted store with shared tasks and one task per writer
When 8 writer processes at once each run 100 mixed comment, update and close writes on it
Then every write the store acknowledged with ok true is held afterwards — each comment exactly once, each close with its reason, each writer's last update — and none is lost
triggeringEvent: t-1831: five processes wrote the live store at once and about 20 of ~450 acknowledged writes were missing afterwards
evidence: src/sqlite-store.ts run() before this criterion: load() outside any transaction, then persist() of the whole state; reproduced at 442 lost of 773 acknowledged (8 writers x 100, test/concurrency.ts)
